kept.spine: The Elected Reeve at Hochhausen has neither the town's backing nor its hostility, and a hard decision here would have to be paid for out of a purse that is empty.
At Hochhausen, the Elected Reeve holds a good name, and the accounts are the reason, since the town is doing well and a town doing well rarely looks hard at who is arranging it.
The hall at Hochhausen is settled, since the Elected Reeve holds it and the town expects it to go on holding it, and business here is conducted on that expectation.
Nothing at Hochhausen governs cleanly, since the Elected Reeve is an arrangement between kinds of power, and it decides at the pace of whichever of them is least willing.

kept.poolKey: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
kept.spine: What governs Hochhausen calls itself the Elected Reeve, and the name says more about the town's own size and self-regard than a stranger usually credits.
Hochhausen has people who would take the hall if they could, and cannot, and every side understands the arrangement precisely for what it is.

kept.poolKey: legitimacyHold: public opinion neither helps nor hurts
kept.spine: Public opinion neither backs the Elected Reeve nor moves against it, and the Elected Reeve governs on the strength of the office alone, favoured no more than it is opposed.
